# PLS-DA Evaluation
## Set up the data for analysis
```{r}
## Import all results
initial_data <- list(
    "all_binary_don" = read.csv("results/triangle/mixed_all/plsda_1000_all.csv"),
    "all_binary_total_don" = read.csv("results/triangle/total_don/mixed_all/plsda_total_don_all.csv"),
    "all_weighted_don" = read.csv("results/triangle/mixed_all/weighted_plsda_1000_all.csv"),
    "all_weighted_total_don" = read.csv("results/triangle/total_don/mixed_all/weighted_plsda_total_don_all.csv"),
    "austrian_binary_don" = read.csv("results/triangle/austrian/plsda_1000_all.csv"),
    "austrian_binary_total_don" = read.csv("results/triangle/total_don/austrian/plsda_total_don_all.csv"),
    "austrian_weighted_don" = read.csv("results/triangle/austrian/weighted_plsda_1000_all.csv"),
    "austrian_weighted_total_don" = read.csv("results/triangle/total_don/austrian/weighted_plsda_total_don_all.csv")
)

# remove all column except 1 - 5 and 15
data <- lapply(initial_data, function(df) df[, c(1:6, 11:14, 18,19)])

# add details about the sample_weight
data <- Map(function(df, nm) {
  df$Sample_weight <- if (grepl("weighted", nm, ignore.case = TRUE)) {
    "True"
  } else {
    "False"
  }
  df
}, data, names(data))

## add details about the dataset
data <- Map(function(df, nm) {
  df$Dataset <- if (grepl("austrian", nm, ignore.case = TRUE)) {
    "Austrian"
  } else {
    "All"
  }
  df
}, data, names(data))

# combine all dataframes into one
combined_data <- do.call(rbind, data)

#Add TPR and TNR
combined_data$TPR <- combined_data$TP / (combined_data$TP + combined_data$FN)
combined_data$TNR <- combined_data$TN / (combined_data$TN + combined_data$FP)

#rename the columns and dataframe for better readability
library(dplyr)
lme_data <- combined_data %>%
 rename(
   Grinding = Sample_source,
   Toxin = Target_toxin,
   Weighting = Sample_weight,
   Downsampling = Downsampled
 ) %>%
  mutate(
    Grinding = case_when(
      Grinding == "intact" ~ "False",
      Grinding == "ground" ~ "True",
      TRUE ~ as.character(Grinding)
    ),
    Toxin = case_when(
      Toxin == "Total_DON" ~ "Total DON",
      TRUE ~ as.character(Toxin)
    ),
    Preprocessing = case_when(
      Preprocessing == "1st_Der" ~ "FD",
      TRUE ~ as.character(Preprocessing)
    ),
    Downsampling = case_when(
      Downsampling %in% c("TRUE", TRUE) ~ "True",
      Downsampling %in% c("FALSE", FALSE) ~ "False",
      TRUE ~ as.character(Downsampling)
    )
  )

# except F1_Score, TPR, TNR and MCC, transform all to factor
lme_data[c(1:6, 13,14)] <- lapply(lme_data[c(1:6, 13,14)], as.factor)
str(lme_data)
```

## Analysis using Linear mixed-effects on F1-Score
This experiment is performed using Full Factorial Design with 6 factors: Grinding, Toxin, Preprocessing, Variable_Selection, Downsampling, Dataset and Weighting. The model includes all main effects and interactions up to the three-way level. The random effect is Split, which accounts for the variability across different data splits.

```{r}
# Load necessary libraries
library(glmmTMB)
library(car)
library(emmeans)

# The F1_Score is a proportion, so we can use a beta regression with logit link function. However, since we have random effects, we will use glmmTMB which can handle beta regression with random effects.
model_f1 <- glmmTMB(F1_score ~ Dataset + Downsampling + Grinding + Toxin + Weighting + Preprocessing + Variable_Selection + (1|Split), data = lme_data, 
family = ordbeta(link = "logit"), control = glmmTMBControl(optCtrl = list(iter.max = 1000, eval.max = 1000)))

Anova(model_f1, type = "II") # All main effects are significant.
summary(model_f1)

# Get marginal means for all combinations
pipeline_means_f1 <- emmeans(model_f1, 
                          ~ Grinding * Toxin * Preprocessing * 
                            Variable_Selection * Downsampling * 
                            Dataset * Weighting)

# Convert to dataframe and back-transform to probability scale
pipeline_df_f1 <- as.data.frame(pipeline_means_f1) %>%
  mutate(
    pipeline = paste(Grinding, Toxin, Preprocessing,
                     Variable_Selection, Downsampling,
                     Dataset, Weighting, sep = " | "),
    F1_est   = plogis(emmean),
    F1_lcl   = plogis(asymp.LCL),
    F1_ucl   = plogis(asymp.UCL)
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(F1_est))

```

### Model Validation

```{r}
## Model validation
library(DHARMa)
sim_f1 <- simulateResiduals(model_f1, plot = TRUE)
plot(sim_f1)
## the KS test is notoriously hyper-sensitive. These are your exact F1 scores of 0 and 1. DHARMa frequently flags these boundary values as "outliers" because the observed data hit those exact floors and ceilings slightly more (or less) often than the simulated data expected. It is a mathematical artifact of the simulation process, not a failure of your model.
plotResiduals(sim_f1, form = lme_data$Grinding)
## Perfect symmetry, the levene test is not significant.
# determine the ICC (intraclass correlation) of the model
library(performance)
library(see)
library(ggplot2)
icc(model_f1)
r2(model_f1) #explain 71.4% of the variance in F1 score
check_collinearity(model_f1) # there is no collinearity issue in the model
pp_check <- check_predictions(model_f1)
pp <- plot(pp_check) + theme_classic()
pp
ggsave("./figures/PLS_DA/total_don/f1_prediction_check.svg", pp, width = 7, height = 5, dpi = 300) # prediction fit well with the observed data

```

### Plotting for each factor

```{r}
source("utils/plotting.R")
effects <- c("Grinding", "Toxin", "Preprocessing", "Variable_Selection", "Downsampling", "Dataset", "Weighting")

effect_plots <- list()
effect_plots <- lapply(effects, function(effect) {
  plot_effect(model_f1, factor = effect, title = paste("Main Effect of", effect, "on F1 Score"))
})
names(effect_plots) <- effects

# Combining all effects into a single plot
library(ggpubr)
combined_effect_plot <- ggarrange(plotlist = 
  effect_plots$Dataset$plot, effect_plots$Downsampling$plot, effect_plots$Grinding$plot, effect_plots$Toxin$plot, effect_plots$Weighting$plot, effect_plots$Preprocessing$plot, effect_plots$Variable_Selection$plot, 
  ncol = 4, nrow = 2, labels = c("A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F", "G"))
combined_effects <- annotate_figure(
  combined_effect_plot,
  top = text_grob(
    "Main Effects of Pipeline Parameters on Estimated F1 Score",     
    color = "black",
    face = "bold",  
    size = 14,
    vjust = 0.5
  )
)
combined_effects
ggsave("./figures/PLS_DA/total_don/f1_main_effects.svg", combined_effects, width = 12, height = 6, dpi = 300)
```

### Plotting
```{r}
library(ggpubr)
library(viridis)
density_plot <- function(data, var, color, label, title){
  plot <- ggplot(data, aes(x = var, fill = color)) +
    geom_density(alpha = 0.5) +
    theme_classic() +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 5)) +
    labs(title = title, x = label, fill = color) +
    scale_fill_viridis(discrete = TRUE) +
    theme(legend.position = "top",
    legend.title = element_blank())
  return(plot)
}

f1_plot <- density_plot(lme_data, lme_data$F1_score, color = "F1_Score", label = "F1 Score", title = "F1 Score of all pipelines") + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("F1_Score" = "#DBA41A")) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 7))
f1_weighting_plot <- density_plot(lme_data, lme_data$F1_score, lme_data$Weighting, label = "F1 Score", title = "Effect of Weighting") + scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 7))
f1_downsampling_plot <- density_plot(lme_data, lme_data$F1_score, lme_data$Downsampling, label = "F1 Score", title = "Effect of Downsampling") + scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 7))
f1_toxin_plot <- density_plot(lme_data, lme_data$F1_score, lme_data$Toxin, label = "F1 Score", title = "Effect of Toxin") + scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 7))
f1_dataset_plot <- density_plot(lme_data, lme_data$F1_score, lme_data$Dataset, label = "F1 Score", title = "Effect of Dataset") + scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 7))
f1_grinding_plot <- density_plot(lme_data, lme_data$F1_score, lme_data$Grinding, label = "F1 Score", title = "Effect of Grinding") + scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 7))
f1_preprocessing_plot <- density_plot(lme_data, lme_data$F1_score, lme_data$Preprocessing, label = "F1 Score", title = "Effect of Preprocessing") + scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 7))
f1_variable_selection_plot <- density_plot(lme_data, lme_data$F1_score, lme_data$Variable_Selection, label = "F1 Score", title = "Effect of Variable Selection") + scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 7))
f1_plots <- ggarrange(f1_plot, f1_weighting_plot, f1_downsampling_plot, f1_toxin_plot, f1_dataset_plot, f1_grinding_plot, f1_preprocessing_plot, f1_variable_selection_plot,
          ncol = 4, nrow = 2)
ggsave("./figures/PLS_DA/total_don/f1_density_plots.svg", f1_plots, width = 12, height = 6)
```

### FP and FN analysis for the most optimal pipeline

```{r}
# import the csv files
# Load required libraries
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(stringr)
library(readxl)

# 1. Load your results data (adjust the path if necessary)
results_f1 <- list(
  none = read.csv("./results/F1/plsda_1000_all.csv"),
  weighted = read.csv("./results/F1/weighted_plsda_1000_all.csv"))

# 2. Extract and separate the FP and FN samples into a long format
# This splits the "Sample_A; Sample_B" strings into individual rows
missclassified_samples <- lapply(results_f1, function(df) {
  fp_df <- df %>%
    select(Split, FP_Samples) %>%
    filter(FP_Samples != "", !is.na(FP_Samples)) %>%
    separate_rows(FP_Samples, sep = ";\\s*") %>%
    rename(Sample_ID = FP_Samples) %>%
    mutate(Misclassification = "False Positive (FP)")
  
  fn_df <- df %>%
    select(Split, FN_Samples) %>%
    filter(FN_Samples != "", !is.na(FN_Samples)) %>%
    separate_rows(FN_Samples, sep = ";\\s*") %>%
    rename(Sample_ID = FN_Samples) %>%
    mutate(Misclassification = "False Negative (FN)")
  
  bind_rows(fp_df, fn_df)
})

y <- read_excel("data/nirs_intact.xlsx") %>% dplyr::select(c("Sample_ID", "Deoxynivalenol"))
missclassified_samples <- lapply(missclassified_samples, function(df) {
  df %>%
    inner_join(y, by = "Sample_ID") %>%
    mutate(
      Uncertainty = case_when(
        Deoxynivalenol < 700 ~ "False Positive (FP)",
        Deoxynivalenol > 1300 ~ "False Negative (FN)",
        Deoxynivalenol < 1000 ~ "Uncertain False Positive (UFP)",
        TRUE ~ "Uncertain False Negative (UFN)"
      ),
      Uncertainty = factor(Uncertainty, levels = c("False Positive (FP)", "Uncertain False Positive (UFP)", "Uncertain False Negative (UFN)", "False Negative (FN)"))
    )
})

sum(missclassified_samples$none$Misclassification == "False Negative (FN)")
sum(missclassified_samples$weighted$Misclassification == "False Negative (FN)")

# 4. Create a histogram plot
source("utils/plotting.R")
missclassified_plot <- lapply(missclassified_samples, function(df){
  hist_plot(df)
})
misclassified_plot$none
misclassified_plot$weighted
```


## Analysis using Linear mixed-effects on TPR and TNR
 
 ```{r}
 # Data analysis for TPR
model_tpr <- glmmTMB(TPR ~ Grinding + Toxin + Preprocessing + Variable_Selection + Downsampling + Dataset + Weighting + (1|Split), data = lme_data, family = ordbeta(link = "logit"),
control = glmmTMBControl(optCtrl = list(iter.max = 1000, eval.max = 1000)))
Anova(model_tpr, type = "II")
summary(model_tpr)

# determine the ICC (intraclass correlation) of the model
library(performance)
icc(model_tpr)
r2(model_tpr)

```

### Model validation for TPR

```{r}
## Model validation
library(DHARMa)
sim_tpr <- simulateResiduals(model_tpr, plot = TRUE)
plot(sim_tpr)
## the KS test is notoriously hyper-sensitive. These are your exact TPR scores of 0 and 1. DHARMa frequently flags these boundary values as "outliers" because the observed data hit those exact floors and ceilings slightly more (or less) often than the simulated data expected. It is a mathematical artifact of the simulation process, not a failure of your model.
plotResiduals(sim_tpr, form = lme_data$Grinding)
## Perfect symmetry, the levene test is not significant.
# determine the ICC (intraclass correlation) of the model
library(performance)
library(see)
icc(model_tpr)
r2(model_tpr) #explain 91.1% of the variance in TPR score
check_collinearity(model_tpr) # there is no collinearity issue in the model
pp_check_tpr <- check_predictions(model_tpr)
plot(pp_check_tpr) # prediction fit well with the observed data
```
